Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded a Total Net Outflow of $89.8978 Million on October 5 According to data from SoSoValue, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a total net outflow of $89.8978 million on October 5 (EDT), with BlackRock's IBIT being the sole fund to see net inflows. Meanwhile, spot Ethereum ETFs saw a total net inflow of $111 million yesterday, with BlackRock's ETHA also being the only fund to register net inflows. — link

Ethereum Economic Zone: First Atomic L1-to-L2 Mainnet Transaction Executed Eduardo Antuña, a core contributor to the Ethereum Economic Zone (EEZ), announced on social media that the first-ever atomic cross-chain L1-to-L2 transaction has been executed on the Ethereum mainnet. Antuña emphasized that atomic synchronous composability is no longer merely theoretical, noting that this milestone represents just the beginning for EEZ's roadmap in bridging seamless cross-layer execution across the Ethereum ecosystem. — link

Highlight Clip: Vitalik: AI Will Become the New UI Vitalik: AI Will Become the New UI On October 6, 2026, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said at OKX NOW in Singapore that AI will become the new user interface in more and more scenarios. He shared how a local AI agent wrote a script to update his ENS hash in about five minutes, and said performing complex blockchain operations without a traditional UI will become normal. This could reduce security risks associated with traditional frontends, while introducing new challenges such as prompt injection, AI safety, and whether agents correctly understand onchain operations. — link

Fortitude Mining Plans Up to $100M Purchase of Bitmain’s Next-Generation Zcash Miners Zcash miner Fortitude Mining announced that it has signed a non-binding letter of intent with Bitmain, securing a priority allocation for Bitmain’s next-generation Zcash mining machines and planning to purchase up to $100 million worth of equipment. The miners have not yet been commercially released and are expected to begin shipping in Q2 2027, subject to final specifications, pricing and definitive purchase agreements. Meanwhile, parent company DCG increased Fortitude’s credit facility from $50 million to $70 million. Fortitude plans to draw $20 million this week, funded in ZEC, to cover a refundable deposit. — link
